h1: The 6 Best Cordless Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Lawn Mowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six cordless lawn mowers from 16 to 21 inch decks, covering voltage, battery count, drive type and the lawns each suits.
summary: The EGO Power+ LM2114 is our top pick, a 21-inch 56V mower with battery and charger included. The Greenworks 80V self-propelled is the choice for sloped or larger lawns, and the Greenworks 48V combo kit bundles a trimmer and blower. The SEYVUM adds a spare battery for less.
intro: Cordless mower shoppers often compare voltage and ignore the number that actually sets mowing time: how much energy the battery holds. A 40V mower with a small battery can run out before a 56V mower with a big one, and a spare battery doubles your session at once.

We reviewed six mowers on paper, comparing deck width, battery setup, drive and bundled tools. Battery numbers and owner notes form the basis of the order, since we ran noour own mowing, and prices are buckets. Runtime depends on grass height and terrain, so treat any minute figure you see as a rough guide.

products.name: EGO Power+ 21-Inch Cordless Lawn Mower (LM2114)
products.verdict: A full-width cordless deck with battery and charger in the box.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ LM2114 has a 21 inch deck, a 56V battery platform and a push drive, with the battery and charger included. It sits in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks first because it combines a full-width deck with a 56V platform and no extra purchases, while the Greenworks 80V adds a drive for slopes.

It suits standard-size, mostly flat lawns. The caveat is that push-only means you do the walking effort.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Drive wheels cut the walking effort on bigger lawns.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V is a 21 inch self-propelled mower with an 80V 4Ah battery and charger included. It lands in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks second because the drive reduces effort on large or sloped yards, an advantage over the EGO LM2114, though the EGO uses a larger platform family.

It suits sloped or larger lawns. The caveat is battery size for yards beyond mid-size.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is small and flat.

products.name: Greenworks 48V (24V x 2) 20-Inch Mower, Trimmer, and Blower Combo Kit
products.verdict: Mower, trimmer and blower on one battery system.
products.description:
This Greenworks kit pairs a 20 inch mower on a 48V (24V x 2) battery bay with a string trimmer and a 320 CFM blower. Three batteries and chargers are included. It sits in the $500+ bucket.

It ranks third because the cost is highest, but it replaces three separate purchases. The mower alone is a step below the EGO.

It suits buyers outfitting a whole yard at once. The caveat is price if you only need a mower.
products.idealFor: Outfitting a whole yard at once.

products.name: SEYVUM 40V 16-Inch Cordless Lawn Mower
products.verdict: Two batteries and a 45L bag for less money.
products.description:
The SEYVUM is a 16 inch push mower on a 40V platform with dual 4Ah batteries and a 45L collection bag. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

Fourth position reflects that the spare battery is a real edge over the Greenworks 40V below, though the deck is narrow.

It suits small lawns where long sessions matter. The caveat is the narrow cut.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Cordless Push Mower
products.verdict: A compact mower that shares batteries with Greenworks 40V tools.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V is a 16 inch push mower with a 40V 4Ah battery and charger included. It falls in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks fifth because the SEYVUM offers a second battery for less. Its point is fitting an existing Greenworks 40V collection.

It suits small lawns and current Greenworks owners. The caveat is a price that exceeds its size.
products.skipIf: You want a spare battery included.

products.name: 18-Inch 40V Brushless Cordless Push Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A wide brushless deck at the lowest entry price.
products.description:
This 18 inch push mower uses a 40V brushless motor in a lightweight frame. It sits in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks last because the listing gives no battery details, so runtime is a question mark. The brushless motor and 18 inch deck are the draws.

It suits buyers who want the lowest cost. The caveat is the missing battery information.

whatMatters.detail: Ah measures how much charge a battery holds. Higher Ah means more mowing per charge. Check Ah and whether the battery is included.
Voltage indicates power and tool compatibility. Batteries often fit only one brand's platform. Check what else you own.
A wider deck covers more per pass. 16 inch suits small lawns, 21 inch suits standard ones. Match to lawn size.
Drive wheels pull the mower for you. They help on slopes and big lawns. Check the drive wording.
A second battery lets you keep going while one charges. Some kits include it. Read the box contents.

howToChoose.intro: Lawn size sets the deck and battery you need.

cards.label: Push
cards.text: Push mowers are lighter and cheaper. The EGO LM2114, SEYVUM and both Greenworks 40V and 18 inch models are push.

cards.label: Self-propelled
cards.text: Self-propelled mowers reduce effort on slopes. The Greenworks 80V is the one here.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers with flat lawns should default to push.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A self-propelled drive and a battery big enough for the extra load.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Greenworks 80V self-propelled is the pick for hills.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a full yard of tools or a bigger deck, which means the Greenworks 48V Combo Kit or EGO LM2114.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is small, where the SEYVUM is enough.

faq.q: How long does a cordless mower run?
faq.a: It depends on battery, grass and terrain. A spare battery is the simplest fix.
Comparing voltage alone and ignoring Ah.

faq.q: Is the Greenworks 80V worth it over the EGO?
faq.a: If you have slopes and want drive.
Within the same brand platform, often yes.

faq.q: How do I store the battery?
faq.a: Keep it at moderate temperature and not fully drained.

faq.q: Do cordless mowers handle wet grass?
faq.a: They struggle. Mow when grass is dry.

finalTake: The EGO Power+ LM2114 is the best cordless mower here for standard lawns. The Greenworks 80V is the drive-equipped choice for slopes, and the Greenworks 48V kit covers the whole yard. The SEYVUM is the budget buy with a spare battery. Check battery Ah before anything else.
